acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Nagas family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Serpent Empress, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Relic-Orbit Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Coils fill the frame in four readable rings, the hood fans into a gem-studded crown, a formal headdress frames multiple arms, and four relics orbit on explicit gold tracks.

Signature mechanic: Crown of Four Relics: the gem-studded hood-crown aligns four floating relics on visible gold tracks around the torso. The Dart relic directs Serpentling fire, the Crescent relic arms Coilguard arcs, the Script relic sets an Adept sequence, and the Gate relic closes a Guardian threshold. The Empress's coils fill four concentric lanes, one per relic. When a known pattern resolves, its track hinge opens at the outer coil; breaking it grounds the relic, dismisses that lower form, and forces the corresponding coil ring to unwrap into a straight vulnerable length. At two relics the headdress drops and commands resolve one at a time.
battlefieldDuty: Command a four-relic temple boss whose enormous coils redraw the arena around lower-form stations until broken gold bands ground each orbit and shorten the sovereign body.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 retain no hood and two arms with ember channels confined to arm bands and dorsal scales; T3–T5 retain hood and multiple arms with ceramic vents distributed across existing hood ribs and weapon bands.
Materials and actions become a kiln liturgy through heat-crazed gold, charred silk edges, ceramic fuel beads, sequential hand-to-hand ignition, and a dark cooling scale seam on the outer coil.
counterplay: Use the selected lower-form response, reach the exposed outer-track hinge, and break it; each grounded relic permanently removes one command and opens one concentric lane. Affinity signal: A fuel bead passes through the existing hands and reaches the outer coil before ignition; interrupt that transfer or strike the black cooling seam after release.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only orange scales without kiln materials and sequential fuel routing
Glow-only fire treatment without combustion, vents, and cooling response
Invented early-tier hoods or extra arms to carry fire hardware
Flame replacing the serpent coil, existing hands, or hood
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso rises from a long coiled serpent body; the T1–T2 forms have two arms and no hood, while hood and additional arms begin only at T3.
Emerald, jade, deep teal, gold, bronze, ivory, and jewel-toned scale patterns remain the family palette.
Scale, gold, gemstone inlay, silk sash, and temple stone remain separate readable materials rather than a seamless magical body.
Arm bands, gold scale bands, jeweled brow pieces, sacred script, and later hood crests communicate rank.
Coil direction, weapon-bearing hands, hood angle where present, and exposed scale seams preserve attack and counterplay readability.
telegraph: One hood gem aligns, its relic travels on a visible gold track, the corresponding coil band rises, and the named lower form assumes its familiar posture.
